source.title: Fairness via In-Processing in the Over-parameterized Regime: A Cautionary Tale
source.authors: A. Veldanda; Ivan Brugere; Jiahao Chen; Sanghamitra Dutta; Alan Mishler; Siddharth Garg

record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps model width and measures test error, reporting model-wise double descent in two settings. This tests the same size-sweep and error measure on new datasets and architectures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports baseline test-error curves against width in Figure 1 and test-error curves for MinDiff settings in Figure 2; Figure 2 values are shown only in plots, with text describing negligible test-error impact in the over-parameterized regime. Table 1 reports separate CelebA test-error values by width and MinDiff weight. Training-step plots report primary loss and FNR gap, not test error over epochs; the paper does not sweep sample size. Fairness-constrained test-error results in Figures 4–7 and Tables 2–5 are not rows here because they are a threshold-corrected fairness-constrained measure rather than the ordinary test error in the claim.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps width on baseline (λ=0) models and reports test error. It states that both settings show double descent, with error falling past the interpolation threshold. The sweep mainly serves to locate that threshold for a fairness study, but the curves and Table 1 are the study's own results on model-wise double descent in new settings (Waterbirds, CelebA).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors' claim that over-parameterized models are always better on baseline error is not borne out by their own Table 1: width 5 (4.74) beats width 64 (4.99). Double descent is used mainly to locate the interpolation threshold. The paper's conclusion concerns MinDiff's ineffectiveness in over-parameterized models and the benefit of adding regularizers.
record.recipe_differences: The study sweeps model width and measures test error as in a size-wise double-descent evaluation, but uses Waterbirds and CelebA and architectures including a fixed-feature logistic classifier and ResNet-preact-18; it focuses on MinDiff and fairness.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that MinDiff's effect depends on model regime, MinDiff weight, dataset, batch size, and regularizer. These sensitivities concern fairness or fairness-constrained error, not the baseline double-descent curve.

fits_no_version.finding: Under MinDiff fairness penalties the CelebA width–error curve changes. At λ=0.5 the peak moves to width 7 (5.76). At λ=1.5 the curve is nearly flat (5.40–5.67, within confidence intervals).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An added group-fairness penalty flattens or shifts the model-wise double-descent peak.

record.problems: The baseline double-descent values are presented in figures rather than tabulated. Only two dataset/model settings are described, and the text gives no numerical test-error values for the curve itself.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Fairness-constrained test-error plots and tables were not included because they report threshold-corrected fairness-constrained error rather than the ordinary test-error measure in the claim.

untested.parts: Other architectures and datasets. In CelebA the initial descent below width 5 appears only in the figure, not in tabulated numbers.
No test error over training steps; Figure 3 tracks only training loss and FNR gap.
Only one deep ResNet and one random-features classifier; no classical model classes.
No effective-complexity measure predicting peak location.
No label-noise manipulation, no multiple peaks, and no test of whether tuned regularization removes the peak. The regularizers are evaluated only on fairness-constrained error.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 link for the Waterbirds rows is corrected to V4, since that model is a random-features model with a trained linear classifier. The MinDiff (λ>0) rows are unlinked as fairness-penalised training. In CelebA the second descent does not recover below the smallest under-parameterized model's error within the tested widths, which a reader comparing magnitudes should note. I chose tranche T3 because the double-descent result is incidental to a fairness study on new datasets.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests model-width behavior in its Waterbirds and CelebA settings, not other datasets or architectures.
No test-error curve over training epochs or steps is reported.
Training sample size is not varied.
The curve is examined in two settings, not broadly across model classes or tasks.
No single effective-complexity measure is evaluated as a predictor of peak location across axes.

The study does not test whether label noise or variance drives the peak, whether multiple peaks occur, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes it. Its regularization experiments concern fairness-constrained error.
The study does not re-count complexity using an effective number of parameters or test whether that produces an ordinary U-shaped curve.

relationships.condition: CelebA, ResNet-preact-18 width sweep, baseline (λ=0) training
relationships.reason: Error peaks at 5.52 at width 13, near the threshold of 11, then falls to 4.98–4.99 at widths 55–64. The authors state double descent explicitly (f1-ce, t1-*-l0).
relationships.display_finding: Error peaked at 5.52 at width 13, near the interpolation threshold of 11, then decreased to 4.98–4.99 at widths 55–64.
